lesson.text: Quick memory: last unit, cells. What is a cell? The smallest unit of life: every living thing is made of cells.
Your body is organised in levels: cells make tissues, tissues make organs, and organs work together in organ systems.
The circulatory system (heart, blood and blood vessels) carries oxygen and food around the body. The respiratory system (the lungs) takes in oxygen and gets rid of carbon dioxide.
The digestive system breaks food down so the blood can carry it. The skeletal and muscular systems hold you up and move you. The nervous system (brain and nerves) sends messages.
Systems work together: when you run, your muscles need more oxygen, so you breathe faster and your heart beats faster.
Try it in the world: sprint across your world, then stop and feel your heartbeat and your breathing. Which two systems are working harder together? Next: the skeleton and muscles.

exercises.prompt: Which organ pumps blood around the body?
exercises.hint: Feel it beat.
exercises.explain: The heart pumps blood.

exercises.prompt: Which system includes the lungs?
exercises.hint: Which system do you use to breathe?
exercises.explain: The lungs are in the respiratory system.

exercises.prompt: Organs are made of tissues.
exercises.hint: Put the levels in order from the smallest: cells, then tissues. What comes next?
exercises.explain: Yes: tissues build organs.

exercises.prompt: Which system breaks down food?
exercises.hint: It starts in your mouth.
exercises.explain: The digestive system breaks food down.

exercises.prompt: Which organ is the control centre of the nervous system?
exercises.hint: Which organ do you think with?
exercises.explain: The brain controls the nervous system.

exercises.prompt: Order from smallest to largest.
exercises.hint: Start with the smallest unit of life.
exercises.explain: Cells, tissues, organs, then organ systems.

exercises.prompt: What does blood carry to the muscles?
exercises.hint: Muscles need fuel.
exercises.explain: Blood carries oxygen and food.

exercises.prompt: Which two systems work together to get oxygen to your muscles?
exercises.hint: Breathing in, then carrying it.
exercises.explain: The lungs take oxygen in; the blood carries it.

exercises.prompt: The skeletal and muscular systems work together to move you.
exercises.hint: Muscles pull on bones.
exercises.explain: Yes: muscles pull on bones to move you.

exercises.prompt: Which system sends messages between the brain and the body?
exercises.hint: Which system is made of the brain and nerves?
exercises.explain: The nervous system carries messages.

exercises.prompt: When you run, why do you breathe faster?
exercises.hint: What do working muscles need more of, that you breathe in?
exercises.explain: Faster breathing brings in more oxygen for your muscles.

exercises.prompt: Food is broken down in the digestive system. How does it reach your muscles?
exercises.hint: Which system carries things around?
exercises.explain: The circulatory system carries food in the blood.

exercises.prompt: Each body system works completely alone.
exercises.hint: Think of running.
exercises.explain: No: body systems work together.

exercises.prompt: Which one is an organ?
exercises.hint: An organ is made of tissues.
exercises.explain: The stomach is an organ; a blood cell is a cell; the digestive system is a system.

exercises.prompt: What happens to your heart rate during exercise?
exercises.hint: Muscles need more blood.
exercises.explain: Your heart beats faster to send more blood.

exercises.prompt: Match each system to its job.
exercises.hint: Think of the main organ in each: heart, lungs, stomach, brain.
exercises.explain: Circulatory: carries blood. Respiratory: takes in oxygen. Digestive: breaks down food. Nervous: sends messages.

exercises.prompt: Sort each one: a cell, an organ or a system?
exercises.hint: Cells are the tiniest; organs are parts like the heart; a system is many organs working together.
exercises.explain: Red blood cells and nerve cells are cells. The heart and the stomach are organs. The digestive and nervous systems are systems.

exercises.prompt: Sort the organs into their systems.
exercises.hint: Does it move blood, air or food?
exercises.explain: Circulatory: the heart and the blood vessels move blood. Respiratory: the lungs and the windpipe move air. Digestive: the stomach and the intestines break down food.

exercises.prompt: Order how oxygen gets from the air to a running leg muscle.
items: The blood carries it round the body.
You breathe air into your lungs.
The muscle uses it to release energy.
exercises.hint: Start with breathing in, then follow the oxygen into the blood and on.
exercises.explain: You breathe air into your lungs, oxygen passes into the blood, the heart pumps the blood round the body, and the leg muscle uses the oxygen to release energy from food.

exercises.prompt: Match each job in a sprint to the system that does it.
exercises.hint: Ask which part of the body does each job: the heart, the lungs, muscles and bones, or the brain?
exercises.explain: Pumping more blood: circulatory (the heart). Breathing faster: respiratory (the lungs). Moving the legs: muscles pulling on bones. Telling them to move: the nervous system.
